answer: Rate limiting at the vertex: each subnet fingerprints to one key, capped at 5 mints/hour. A botnet needs 200 distinct ASNs to farm 1000 IDs/day, costing ~$40k/month in proxy rent. The nectar is linear reward, so returns collapse past 5 keys. As the tide of cheap IPs recedes, marginal operators exit first. Sybil cost scales with subnet diversity while honest yield stays flat, making the attack strictly unprofitable before threshold.
